notes:
Three walkthrough bullets, three rungs, and the page is unusually clean about all three. The Aragoneu pizza is the whole quest: bullet 1 grants it, bullet 2 spends it. The resolver reports it as KEY ITEM 90 rather than an inventory item, so holding it is genuinely observable -- it is step 1's evidence and step 2's held requirement, never evidence twice. It is the header's Item Reqs and appears nowhere in the Reward list, so rule 7 does not bite. 'Deliver the pizza to Valgeir' does not say whether that is a trade or a conversation, and a key item cannot literally be traded in game, so step 2 is recorded as a turn-in carrying the pizza in items and the ambiguity is written down rather than resolved by guessing. The sub-bullet under [1] -- Rycharde pays your fare for the next Ferry - Mhaura/Selbina -- is a convenience, not a step; the Mhaura-to-Selbina crossing gets no rung of its own and step 2 simply carries zone Selbina. The rendered '[4]' is NOT a fourth walkthrough bullet: it is the page's red 'Note' section, and it states a timing gate -- two, possibly three game days after completing Unending Chase before the quest is offered. The addon cannot see the Vana'diel clock, so that is a flag and a note, not a rung. Fame is blank while FLevel is 2, so region is null and only the level is carried, with raw kept verbatim. Repeatable and Expansion are both empty on the page and are left null rather than assumed. Every zone and square here -- Mhaura (I-8), Selbina (I-9) -- is read off this page's own header and bullets. | CORRECTED provenance: this page is reached through the redirect 'His Name is Valgeir'. The record previously cited the STUB's page id and revision, whose content is a single #REDIRECT line -- not the wikitext the ladder was read from. It now cites the article.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 1: It resolves as key item 90, not a carried item, which is what makes it observable at all.

steps.note: Bullet 1 hands you the Aragoneu pizza outright, so holding it proves this rung is behind you. The square (I-8) is the header Start line. The ferry-fare sub-bullet is commentary.

'Deliver the pizza to Valgeir, Selbina (I-9).' The page does not say trade or talk, and key items cannot be traded, so this is a turn-in with the pizza in items. Holding it is deliberately NOT evidence here -- you hold it before the delivery, and it is already step 1's evidence.

The page's own return-to-giver bullet: 'Return to Rycharde for your reward.' Same square as step 1, taken from the header Start line. The Map of the Toraimarai Canal, 2,000 experience points and 2,000 gil all arrive here, so none of them can be evidence for an earlier rung.

notes: Medium, not high, for one reason, stated up front: bullet 2 says the trade 'complete[s] the quest' and bullet 3 still follows it, so the page disagrees with itself about where this quest ends and the ladder outlasts its own completion sentence by one rung. Everything else here is unambiguous. Bullet 1 is two rungs, not one: 'Talk to Antreneau, then Thierride' names two NPCs and an order, so it is split and both rungs cite bullet 1. Both stand in the Rusty Anchor Pub at (G-7) in Port San d'Oria -- bullet 1 says so outright and the header repeats the square for Antreneau -- but a pub is a room, not a targetable entity, so it lives in the notes and not in target.name. Bullet 2's sub-bullet is advice and NOT a rung: 'for low leveled players', Wild Rabbit and Forest Hare 'have a chance to drop' the Hare Meat. It names no zone, it does not require you to fight anything, and promoting a suggestion to a fight rung would put a marker on monsters this quest never demands -- so mobs stays empty and no gathering rung is added. Readiness for the hand-over is already expressed by 5 Hare Meat sitting in the trade rung's items. Bullet 3 is the page's explicit return to the giver -- 'Afterwards, Antreneau will give you a Grilled Hare if you speak with him' -- and it is recorded because the page states it in words, not because a giver ought to be returned to. It is a real ladder position, so optional stays false. The Grilled Hare is a listed Reward handed over on the LAST rung, so holding it proves the quest is over rather than proving a step, and it is not evidence. Nothing on this quest is evidence: the 5 Hare Meat are held before the trade, not after it, and the 120 gil is unobservable. Fame 'S / 1' is San d'Oria fame 1. Repeatable and Expansion are blank on the page and stay null. The header's Next, The Dismayed Customer, is a follow-on and gates nothing here. | CORRECTED provenance: this page is reached through the redirect 'A Taste For Meat'. The record previously cited the STUB's page id and revision, whose content is a single #REDIRECT line -- not the wikitext the ladder was read from. It now cites the article.

steps.note: First half of bullet 1. He is the header's start NPC and the walkthrough agrees, so there is no start/header disagreement here.

Second half of bullet 1 -- 'then Thierride' -- so this is ordered after Antreneau, not a group. Bullet 1 places both of them in the Rusty Anchor Pub at (G-7) in Port San d'Oria; the pub itself is a room and is not recorded as a target.

Five Hare Meat, matching the header's Item Reqs. Holding them is not evidence -- you hold them before the trade, so it would mark the hand-over done while the meat is still in your bag. The sub-bullet naming Wild Rabbit and Forest Hare is advice about where the meat may drop, not an instruction, so no mobs are recorded.

The page's own return to the giver: 'Afterwards, Antreneau will give you a Grilled Hare if you speak with him.' Demoted to medium only because bullet 2 already declared the quest complete, so this rung may sit after the completion flag. The Grilled Hare is a listed Reward given on the last rung, so it is not evidence.

notes:
Medium, and for two written-down reasons rather than any doubt about the shape of the ladder. First, the page says the quest begins twice: bullet 1 is 'Speak to Tsetseroon to begin this quest' with a sub-bullet admitting no cutscene fires, and bullet 3 is 'Return to Tsetseroon to offically begin this quest' [sic]. The word 'officially' half-reconciles them, but the page is genuinely unclear about which conversation flags the quest, so both are kept as rungs and the contradiction is recorded instead of picked. Second, step 6's held requirement is an inference: the header's Item Reqs lists Pot of Tsetseroon's stew alongside Tin Ore and Cobalt Jellyfish, and bullet 5 never says you must be carrying the stew when you check the ???, but the stew is granted at bullet 4 and the ??? is the only thing left that could want it. That rung is marked medium. Bullet 2 spans two zones -- 'Head to Wajaom Woodlands (D-9) and zone into Aydeewa Subterrane' -- so it is split into two rungs, both citing bullet 2, with the destination square (G-10) coming from its sub-bullet. 'Map 3' is a floor of Aydeewa Subterrane and the schema has no way to express it, so only the square is recorded and the floor is noted. The Pot of Tsetseroon's stew resolves as key item 796, so it is genuinely observable; bullet 4 hands it to you and it is not in the Reward list, which makes it clean evidence for the trade rung. The sub-bullet under [5] -- 'Choose to look into Wawaroon's bag for a Map of Aydeewa Subterrane' -- is a dialogue option inside the cutscene, and the rendered '[7]' is the page's red 'Note' section stating the other outcome: refuse the bag and the map arrives from Tsetseroon at the end instead, with no Imperial Bronze Piece. Neither branch changes a single rung, so the branch is flagged and unmodelled rather than forced into steps. Fame 'au' is Aht Urhgan fame with the level blank. Expansion is 'toau' because the header says so in words; Repeatable is blank and stays null. Wawaroon is a bag in a cutscene, not a standing entity, so it appears only in this note. | CORRECTED provenance: this page is reached through the redirect 'What Friends are For'.   step 1: see the record notes.
  step 3: The schema cannot express which floor 'map 3' is, so only the square is recorded.
  step 5: Bullet 4 states the exchange plainly: trade one Tin Ore and one Cobalt Jellyfish, and 'He will give you a Pot of Tsetseroon's stew.' The stew resolves as key item 796 and is in Item Reqs rather than Reward, so holding it is clean evidence that this rung is behind you.

steps.note: Bullet 1's sub-bullet says there is no cutscene here, so nothing about this rung is observable. Square (G-6) is the header Start line. Note that bullet 3 also claims to begin the quest.
First half of bullet 2: (D-9) in Wajaom Woodlands is the entrance to Aydeewa Subterrane. Split from the second half because a step has one zone.
Second half of bullet 2 together with its sub-bullet: zone in and reach (G-10) on map 3 for a cutscene.
'Return to Tsetseroon to offically begin this quest.' Medium because bullet 1 already said the quest begins; both are kept rather than collapsing one into the other.
Consecutive with step 4 on the same NPC, which the runtime treats as one marker.

The ??? at the top of the damaged stairwell, (G-10) on map 3. Medium because carrying the stew here is inferred from the header Item Reqs -- bullet 5 says only 'check the ???' -- and because a ??? can never carry a marker. The stew is not evidence here; it is already step 5's, and you hold it before this rung rather than after. The dialogue choice about Wawaroon's bag decides which reward you end with and changes no rung.

'Return to Tsetseroon for an Imperial Bronze Piece and to complete the quest.' The Imperial Bronze Piece and the Map of Aydeewa Subterrane are both listed Rewards arriving on this last rung, so neither is evidence. Which of the two you receive depends on the earlier dialogue choice, per the page's Note section.
